§ 3NATIONAL PARKS

Conservation Sites

  • Areas that are legally protected to preserve their natural or cultural significance are called "protected areas", which can include national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, biosphere reserves, and cultural heritage sites.

Different Conservation Sites

In-Situ ConservationEx-Situ Conservation
Conserving the wildlife in the natural habitatConserving the wildlife outside their natural habitat
E.g. National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuary, Biosphere ReservesE.g. Zoo/Zoological gardens, Aquarium, Botanical gardens

National Park, Wildlife Sanctuary, and Biosphere Reserve

#### National Park

  • A national park is a protected area of land that is managed by the government to preserve the natural environment.
  • They prohibit activities like hunting, deforestation, and industrialisation.

#### Wildlife Sanctuary

  • A wildlife sanctuary is a protected area of land where plants (flora) and animals (fauna) can live and thrive.
  • It is established to protect endangered species and their habitats.
  • They can be owned by the government or a nonprofit organization.

#### Biosphere Reserve

  • These are large area of protected land for conservation of wildlife, plants, animals, and traditional life of the tribals living in the area.

#### Biosphere Reserve Zones

  • There are three zones of Biosphere: Core zone, Buffer zone and Transition zone
  • Core Zone: In this zone, human intervention is strictly prohibited to preserve the natural ecosystem and its biodiversity.
  • Buffer Zone: The buffer zone is the area surrounding the core zone. Humans are permitted to conduct only research and education related work. These activities should not interfere with the core area's conservation goals.
  • Transition Zone: It is a biosphere reserve's periphery where human activities such as cropping, recreation, forestry, and settlements are permitted with the cooperation of reserve management and local people.

International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)

  • HQ: Gland, Switzerland
  • Established in: 1948
  • IUCN maintains a Red Data Book (it records endangered species to raise awareness and protect biodiversity).

Wildlife Protection Act 1972

  • It is an Act of the Parliament of India enacted for the protection of plants and animal species.
  • The act has played a critical role in conserving the country's diverse wildlife.

#### Schedules under this Act

  • Total: 6 schedules
  • Schedule I: It covers endangered species that need rigorous protection → Black buck, snow leopard, Asiatic cheetah, etc.
  • Schedule II: Animals under this list are also accorded high protection with the prohibition on their trade → Indian cobra, Assam Macaque, Himalayan black bear, etc.
  • Schedule III & IV: Species that are not endangered → Sambar deer, chital, etc. (Schedule III) and Crabs, Flamingo, etc. (Schedule IV).
  • Schedule V: This schedule contains animals that are considered as vermin (small wild animals that carry disease and destroy plants and food) → Fruit bat, rats, common crow, etc.
  • Schedule VI: It provides for regulation in the cultivation of a specified plant and restricts its possession, sale, and transportation → Blue orchid, red orchid, pitcher plants, etc.

CONSERVATION SITES — Representation in Maps

  • NP: National Parks (represented in red ♦)
  • WLS: Wildlife Sanctuary (represented in green ♦)
  • BR: Biosphere Reserve (represented in blue ♦)
  • RS: Ramsar Site (represented in purple ♦)
  • TR: Tiger Reserve Lakes (represented in orange ♦)
  • BS: Bird Sanctuary (represented in yellow ♦)
  • Lakes/Jheel: Represented in sky blue ♦

§ 9Key concepts

  • Jim Corbett National Park (First NP of India, 1936; Project Tiger launched 1973; Project Elephant 1992)
  • Kaziranga NP (highest population of one-horned rhinoceros)
  • Gir NP (only habitat of Asiatic Lion; India is the only country with both tigers and lions)
  • Sundarbans NP-BR (home to Royal Bengal Tiger)
  • Keibul-Lamjao NP (world's only floating National Park, on Loktak Lake)
  • Biosphere Reserves (18 total; 12 under UNESCO MAB; three zones: Core, Buffer, Transition)
  • Wildlife Protection Act 1972 (6 schedules covering endangered species, vermin, and plants)
  • IUCN Red Data Book (HQ Gland, Switzerland; established 1948)
